# ADR-0001 · Structural PDF parsing

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-09-07
- **Kind:** Selection
- **Decision:** OPT-3 — A scanner written here that reads only startxref, the trailer dictionary and object delimiters
- **Arises from:** [PDF verification · AC-8](../pdf-service/pdf-verify.md#ac-8), [PDF verification · AC-9](../pdf-service/pdf-verify.md#ac-9)
- **Decides:** [PDF verification · RQ-5](../pdf-service/pdf-verify.md#rq-5)
- **Source:** [`ADR-0001-structural-pdf-parsing.adr.yaml`](../../../trace-fixtures/ADR-0001-structural-pdf-parsing.adr.yaml)

## Question

What reads the cross-reference table, trailer and object structure of an untrusted upload, given that the two failures must be reported as distinct identifiers?

## Forces

- The bytes arrive from an unauthenticated caller (front: external) and are adversarial by default.
- AC-10 fixes a precedence order over seven identifiers, so invalid_xref_trailer and invalid_object_structure must be decidable independently of each other.
- Doing nothing is not available: AC-8 and AC-9 name failures no header/EOF check can detect.
- The service is distributed to customers as a closed-source artifact.

## Decision

**OPT-3** — A scanner written here that reads only startxref, the trailer dictionary and object delimiters

Reversibility: reversible

## Obligations

What the decision obliges the implementation to do.

- **R-1** — Resolve startxref offsets without following them recursively. A cross-reference chain is bounded, or a malformed file can direct it to loop.
- **R-2** — Validate every byte offset read from the file against the file length before using it.
- **R-3** — Keep each check independent of whether another has run. AC-10 evaluates all seven independently, so a scanner that short-circuits cannot report the earliest failure correctly.
- **R-4** — Keep structural parsing of untrusted bytes off the request thread under default JVM limits.

## Accepted costs

- The scanner accepts files a full parser would reject, and rejects none a full parser accepts, only within the four structural properties AC-6 through AC-9 name. It is not a PDF validator.
- Cross-reference streams (PDF 1.5+) need their own decoding path, which is more work than calling a library.

## Revisit when

- A requirement asks for anything inside the page tree — content extraction, rendering, signature verification. The scanner is the wrong shape for it and OPT-1 returns.
- Ownership of the scanner runs past 0.25 engineer-day / month, which is the assumption D-5 rests on.

## Options considered

|  | Option | Reversibility |
|---|---|---|
| OPT-1 | Apache PDFBox 3.x | costly |
| OPT-2 | iText 8 | costly |
| **OPT-3** (chosen) | A scanner written here that reads only startxref, the trailer dictionary and object delimiters | reversible |

### OPT-1 · Apache PDFBox 3.x

References: project <https://pdfbox.apache.org/> · licence <https://github.com/apache/pdfbox/blob/trunk/LICENSE.txt> · failure-modes <https://pdfbox.apache.org/docs/3.0.3/javadocs/org/apache/pdfbox/Loader.html>

- **D-1** — Apache-2.0, no distribution obligation.
- **D-2** — Both failures surface as IOException with library-authored messages. Distinguishing them means matching on message text, which is not a contract.
- **D-3** — A full document model, font and stream decoding are reachable from a parse call; roughly two orders of magnitude more code than the checks need.
- **D-4** — Active, wide deployment, predictable major-version cadence.
- **D-5** (EUR of total ownership) — About 26k, mostly recurring: three engineer-days to adopt, then upgrade and CVE tracking, plus one further service instance to absorb parse-time heap.

### OPT-2 · iText 8

References: project <https://itextpdf.com/products/itext-core> · licence <https://github.com/itext/itext-java/blob/develop/LICENSE.md> · pricing <https://itextpdf.com/how-buy/pricing>

- **D-1** — AGPL-3.0 or a per-seat commercial licence. Blocker under the distribution model.
- **D-2** — n/a — not evaluated, D-1 excludes the option.
- **D-3** — n/a — not evaluated, D-1 excludes the option.
- **D-4** — Active, commercially supported.
- **D-5** (EUR of total ownership) — n/a — not priced, D-1 excludes the option.

### OPT-3 · A scanner written here that reads only startxref, the trailer dictionary and object delimiters (chosen)

References: grammar ISO 32000-1:2008 §7.5

- **D-1** — No third-party licence.
- **D-2** — Each check is a separate function, so the two identifiers fall out of the structure rather than being recovered from a message.
- **D-3** — Reads bytes; builds no document model, decodes no streams, resolves no fonts.
- **D-4** — Maintained here. The PDF structural grammar it depends on is frozen in ISO 32000 and does not move.
- **D-5** (EUR of total ownership) — About 25k, front-loaded: twelve engineer-days to write it and assemble the corpus it is tested against, then low ownership with no dependency to track. Cheaper than OPT-1 only past roughly month 32, so the two are a wash at this horizon.

## Dimensions

What every option was judged against.

- **D-1** — An AGPL obligation on a distributed closed-source artifact is a legal blocker, not a cost. *(source: OSS-policy/distribution.md)*
- **D-2** — AC-8 and AC-9 must map to different identifiers. A parser that collapses both into one generic failure cannot satisfy them without a second mechanism on top.
- **D-3** — Code size reachable from untrusted bytes bounds the damage a malformed upload can do.
- **D-4** — An unmaintained parser is a standing obligation to fork or migrate. *(source: upstream release history and open-issue age)*
- **D-5** — Only decisive at a spread wide enough to survive the engineer-day rate being wrong by a third. *(unit: EUR of total ownership; basis: B-1, B-2; source: cost/pdf-parsing-tco.md, over platform chargeback 2026-H2 and the internal engineer-day rate.)*

## Basis

The quantities the dimensions are stated under.

|  | Quantity | Source |
|---|---|---|
| B-1 | 40000 uploads / month | ingest telemetry, 2026-08 monthly mean |
| B-2 | 36 months | the amortisation horizon this team uses for build-versus-buy |
